app_data.title: Saudi Arabia Theoretical Driving Handbook
app_data.introduction: This handbook is prepared to help trainees obtain a driver's license in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. Driving a vehicle is an important privilege and responsibility. It aims to help you drive safely and prepare for both the practical and theoretical driving test. Information marked in blue in the original book is for personal use and will not be included in the knowledge section of the driver's license test.

units.title: Introduction, Traffic Violations, and Traffic Points

subtopics.title: Private Driving License – Requirements
requirements: Minimum age: 18 years old
Exception: temporary permit for max 1 year can be issued from age 17
Complete the required training in driving schools
Pass the theoretical test and the practical driving test
Pay the prescribed fees
Pay outstanding traffic fines from previous violations

validity.vehicle_types: All kinds of small private vehicles

license_information_fields: Full name of the license holder

subtopics.title: Public Driving License
requirements: Minimum age: 20 years old
Valid for a maximum period of 5 years

categories.name: Taxi Driver License
categories.description: Allows its holder to drive public taxis with a load capacity of no more than 8 people

subtypes.name: Light transport license
subtypes.description: Allows driving small public transport vehicles with total weight not more than 3500 kg

subtypes.name: Heavy transport license
subtypes.description: Allows driving large public or private transport vehicles with total weight more than 3500 kg

subtypes.name: Minibus or private bus license
subtypes.description: Allows driving buses that can carry at least 15 passengers

subtypes.name: Large or public bus license
subtypes.description: Allows driving buses that can carry more than 15 passengers

subtopics.title: Public Works Vehicle Driving License
requirements: Minimum age: 20 years old
Valid for a maximum period of 5 years
Applicant must not have been convicted of crimes of assault of people, honour, or money unless rehabilitated
Applicant must not have been convicted of using, manufacturing, smuggling, distributing, or possessing drugs unless rehabilitated
Regular residency for non-Saudis
No diseases or impairments that prevent driving
Completion of training hours in driving schools and passing the driving test
Paying the prescribed fees
Paying outstanding traffic fines

subtopics.title: Motorcycle Driving License
requirements: Valid for all types of motorbikes
Minimum age: 18 years old
Valid for a maximum of 10 years

subtopics.title: Road Users
key_facts: Pedestrians move at a speed not exceeding 4–5 km/h
Vehicles can move up to 100 km/h
Human emergency high-speed perception starts from 20–30 km/h
Humans are not created to move at high speed, which is why they need technical assistance from the speedometer
Vehicles can move loads from 1500 kg to 3500 kg at high speeds, making collisions very dangerous

subtopics.title: Basic Driving Principles
principles: The driving speed must always be adapted to the surrounding conditions
The driving speed must be chosen such that it is possible to stop in time to avoid a collision with an obstacle and evade other sources of danger

subtopics.title: Stopping Distance
subtopics.definition: The distance the vehicle travels from the moment the driver becomes aware of a dangerous situation until the vehicle comes to a complete stop.
subtopics.formula: Stopping Distance = Reaction Distance + Braking Distance

reaction_distance.definition: The distance traveled by the vehicle from the moment the driver realizes a dangerous situation until applying the brakes.
reaction_distance.note: During this time your car is in motion without decelerating

braking_distance.definition: The distance the vehicle travels from the moment the driver applies the brakes until the vehicle comes to a complete stop.
braking_distance.formula: (Speed/10) × (Speed/10)  (assuming hard braking on a dry road)
braking_distance.note: Distance may be shorter with emergency braking; longer on slippery roads

reaction_distance_increases_when: If you are distracted or tired
If the driver is under the influence of drugs or medications that cause drowsiness
If the driver is under the influence of alcohol
braking_distance_increases_when: When the vehicle load is heavy
Poor road conditions (sand, snow, wet surface)
how_to_reduce_stopping_distance: Increased attention – be prepared to brake; place your foot on the brake pedal without pressing it

example.scenario_1: Traveling at 50 km/h – a truck comes out of an intersection in front of you, you brake hard and stop in time.
example.scenario_2: Traveling at 60 km/h (only 10 km/h faster) – the same truck comes out, you brake hard but cannot stop in time. The truck will be hit at 40 km/h.
example.consequence: If you or a passenger were not wearing seat belts, the physical force would be equivalent to jumping from a third-floor window and hitting the ground after falling 6.5 meters – all because you were driving only 10 km/h faster.

subtopics.title: Statistical Recording
rules: Recorded as INJURY: death occurs more than one month after the accident
Recorded as DEATH: immediate death at accident OR death within one month from the date of occurrence

subtopics.title: Reasons for High Accident Rate in Saudi Arabia
reasons: Failure to comply with traffic laws
Using a mobile phone while driving
Not wearing a seat belt while driving
Failure to take the appropriate course and sudden change of course

criteria: Damage to private or public property not exceeding 5,000 SAR
Personal injury that does not need to be taken to the hospital
Traffic accidents that result in deaths
Serious injuries requiring transfer to hospital and/or operation
Accidents that lead to significant losses in private or public funds

subtopics.title: Legal Liability
subtopics.applies_when: Accident results from negligence, recklessness, or violation of traffic laws

definitions.neglect: Failure to exercise a certain degree of vigilance under circumstances where the law requires the protection of others or their interests
definitions.recklessness: An act committed by the driver indicating default or mismanagement of consequences, showing willful or intentional neglect of law and human life (e.g. driving too fast on a crowded street causing death or injury)
definitions.failure_to_observe_regulations: Failure to comply with the laws in a way that leads to accidents resulting in injuries, deaths, or property damage

subtopics.title: What Every Driver Must Do in a Traffic Accident

actions: Take photographs of the accident from all angles
Park the vehicle away from crowds if possible
Determine the location of the accident, enter the data, and confirm the phone number

report_must_include: A statement of the circumstances and location of the accident
Type of vehicles involved in the accident

subtopics.title: Consequences of Ignoring Accident Laws
penalties: Fine up to 2,000 SAR and/or imprisonment up to 3 months
Leaving the scene without reason = considered a fugitive from justice
when_vehicles_may_be_moved: The vehicle obstructs traffic or poses a threat to public safety
The accident was simple and clear, and both parties agreed on how it happened

accidents_with_death_or_serious_injury.extension: May be extended by the competent court
accidents_with_death_or_serious_injury.release: Must be released immediately if a fine is paid or required insurance policy is presented

subtopics.accidents_caused_by_alcohol_or_drifting: Driver is handed over to the public prosecutor of the competent court to file a lawsuit
subtopics.force_majeure: The penalty may be waived if the accident was caused by force majeure; the driver must explain the circumstances during investigation

topics.title: Traffic Department – Tasks and Importance
topics.identification: Traffic employees can be identified by their uniform or official badge
topics.authority: They represent the state and have the right to enforce the law; their instructions must be followed in all cases
responsibilities: Monitoring the roads and checking driver's licenses
Taking corrective action for traffic violations
Adjusting speed and taking distance measurements
topics.key_rule: Traffic officers can issue orders that conflict with normal traffic regulations. These instructions must be adhered to. Example: if the light is green but the traffic officer tells you to stop, you must stop.

topics.title: Violations and Penalties

violation_procedure.driver_must_remain_inside_vehicle: Until the traffic policeman arrives and completes the violation registration procedures
violation_procedure.violation_copies: Written in 3 copies: one delivered to the violating driver, two sent to the competent authorities
violation_procedure.fine_paper_requirements: Must be filled out and the offending driver must sign it
violation_procedure.if_driver_refuses_to_sign: This must be written in the violation
violation_procedure.if_driver_not_present: The vehicle number plate must be documented and all details added to the violation sheet
violation_procedure.penalty_per_offense: The offending driver will be penalized for each separate offense, even if listed on a single sheet
violation_procedure.inquiry_method: Violations can be inquired about through the Absher website
violation_procedure.automatic_monitoring: Automatically registered violations do not require the above procedure

violation_form_contains.date_time_place: Date, time, and place of the violation
violation_form_contains.payment_period: The period given to pay the fine

paying_the_fine.procedure: The violating driver may pay the minimum fine at the nearest specialized center within 30 days from the date of the violation
paying_the_fine.receipt: An official receipt is issued upon payment
paying_the_fine.if_not_paid_within_30_days: The competent authority shall obligate the offending driver to pay the maximum fine

Leaving the vehicle unlocked and running after leaving it
Lack of valid vehicle insurance
Pedestrians crossing roads other than designated places
Pedestrians not bound by their own signals
Parking the vehicle in places not designated for parking
Not giving priority to pedestrians while crossing their designated lanes
Not using the turn signal when turning right or left, overtaking, or changing lanes

Violation of rules for using convergence lights
Not carrying a driver's license while driving
Misuse of the vehicle alarm
Failure to submit the vehicle for periodic technical inspection
Violation of traffic regulations on the road
Not wearing a seat belt
Placing barriers inside or outside the vehicle that obstruct the driver's vision
Failure to leave sufficient distance between vehicle and the vehicle in front
Moving the vehicle at high speed so that tires make a loud sound
Gathering at the scene of an accident
Overtaking a group of vehicles in front of traffic lights or security control points using the road shoulder or turning lane
Lack of regulatory requirements for a trailer
Failure to take necessary precautions when stopping in emergency on public roads
Throwing objects outside the vehicle
Slowing down in a way that impedes movement
Preoccupation with other than the road while driving
Applying the brakes suddenly and unnecessarily
Non-compliance with traffic regulations at road intersections
Failure to comply with the limits of the specified lanes on the road
Making noise by using devices from inside the vehicle or behavior contrary to public morals while driving
Driving with an expired driver's license
Failure to use child safety seats
Leaving the vehicle on a sloping road without taking necessary precautions

Chasing emergency vehicles while using their sirens
Driving on the road with vehicles designated for acquisition
Not stopping completely at the stop sign
Failure to stop completely at the 'give priority' sign when vehicles are passing on the priority road

Not giving priority to vehicles on the highway in the absence of a priority signal
Not abiding by the hand signals of the traffic police officer and not giving his signals priority over traffic lights
Not giving priority to vehicles inside the roundabout over vehicles outside it in the absence of traffic lights or a traffic officer
Driving inside tunnels without turning on lights
Exceeding cargo dimensions for light transport vehicles beyond the permissible limit
Unnecessarily using emergency vehicle alarms
Not giving priority at junctions or intersections to the driver of the vehicle ahead of others in the absence of regulatory plates
When reversing direction, not giving way to vehicles coming from other directions
When part of the road is closed, not giving preference to those whose road is open
When wishing to change lanes, not giving preference to a vehicle traveling straight when both vehicles are running parallel
Not giving way to vehicles from a highway when intersecting with a secondary road or dirt road
Not giving priority to public transportation (trains, buses) on their designated tracks
Transporting passengers in places not designated for them in the vehicle
Using any portable device while the vehicle is in motion
Parking in parking spaces designated for people with special needs
Placing writing, drawing, sticker, or any statement on the vehicle's body without competent authority approval
Driving a vehicle that pollutes the environment on public roads
Shading the vehicle's windows without complying with regulations
Using the vehicle for a purpose other than that for which it was licensed
Not covering and fixing the carriage
Entry of trucks, heavy equipment and the like into or out of cities at times that are not permitted
Driving a vehicle with a driver's license that does not match the vehicle's size and type of use
Standing on railway tracks
Carrying more passengers than the number specified in the driving license
Refusal to present the driver's or vehicle's documents to authorized persons
Driving a vehicle with unclear or damaged license plates
The vehicle is running without a front panel
Failure to complete the procedures for modifying the area of use of the vehicle
Not taking out the vehicle intended for export within the specified period
Not wearing a helmet while riding a motorcycle
Driving a vehicle before obtaining a driver's license or when the license is withdrawn
Leaving objects on public roads that endanger public safety
Not giving way to official or emergency procession vehicles
Driving on the shoulders of the road, on sidewalks, or on paths where driving is prohibited
Disembarking or riding while vehicles are in motion
Pedestrian crossing of highways
Overtaking in areas where overtaking is prohibited, such as curves and hills
Lack of side lighting, reflectors, or screens for trucks and trailers
Not using necessary lights when walking at night or in conditions where visibility is not clear
Failure to install the panel in its designated place
Gathering at drifting sites
Exceeding cargo dimensions for heavy transport vehicles beyond the permissible limit
Making modifications or additions to the vehicle's body or structure that change its features or basic equipment without following legal procedures
Driving a vehicle without necessary equipment such as brakes, lights, and the like
Use of plates not issued by the competent department
Crossing a red traffic light at speed
Overtaking school transport buses when they stop for loading or unloading
Tampering with road signs, reflectors, or signs regulating traffic

Driving the vehicle in the opposite direction of traffic
Dribbling quickly between vehicles on public roads
Carrying out a vehicle race on public roads or marching in processions without obtaining a permit beforehand
Failure of trucks and heavy equipment to drive in the right lane on multi-lane roads
Animal owners not keeping animals away from approved road precincts
Installing equipment in the vehicle such as those for official vehicles and emergency vehicles

Driving the vehicle without a back plate or without plates
Blurring of vehicle plates
Driving a vehicle under the influence of intoxicants, narcotics, or drugs
Carrying out road works before coordinating with the concerned department
Animal owners allowing animals to cross from places other than those designated for them, or without coordination with the competent authorities
Use of plates that do not belong to the vehicle

violation_tables.title: Speed Violation Fines
violation_tables.legal_reference: Traffic Law issued by Royal Decree No. (M/115) dated 05/12/1439

drifting_penalties.penalty: Vehicle impounded for 15 days + fine of 20,000 SAR + authorities must consider imprisoning the driver
Vehicle impounded for one month + fine of 40,000 SAR + authorities must consider imprisoning the driver
Confiscation of the vehicle + fine of 60,000 SAR

topics.drifting_notes: Rented or stolen vehicles will not be confiscated, but a fine must be paid in the value of the rented or stolen vehicle

topics.driving_during_withdrawal: If caught driving during the revocation period, the driver is treated as not holding a license and referred to the competent court to double the penalty. Driver may be directed to attend a 15-day rehabilitation program at a driving school.
topics.after_permanent_revocation: A new license can be applied for one year after the date of the license revocation, provided the driver has completed a one-month rehabilitation program at a driving school and passed the theory and practical tests.

topics.title: Road Parts

road_definitions.definition: A road that is accessed and exited through entrances and exits and does not directly serve real estate
A geographic area located within the city designated within the road network
The road network outside the cities and towns
A small and elevated area that works to divide movement in two different directions
A lane change that allows traffic to be incorporated into a regular road or motorway
Any intersection, crossing, or branching of roads on one or more levels, including the area formed as a result
Marked with a mandatory traffic light for cyclists
Marked by a mandatory traffic light for horseback riders
Part of the road intended for pedestrian use and not for vehicles
A specific part of the road that pedestrians are entitled to cross; may be marked with white markings and/or traffic lights

intersection_types: Regulated by a traffic officer (hand signals)
Uncontrolled – without any marks, governed by priority law

pedestrian_crossing_signal_rules.continuous_green: Pedestrians are allowed to cross the road but need to monitor traffic
pedestrian_crossing_signal_rules.blinking_green: Signal will soon turn red; pedestrians already crossing must speed up; pedestrians approaching must wait and not enter the lane
pedestrian_crossing_signal_rules.red_or_orange: Pedestrians are not allowed to cross

without_traffic_lights: Drivers must slow down as fast as possible
Must stop in front of the pedestrian crossing if pedestrians want to cross
The safety of pedestrians must not be endangered while they are in transit
with_traffic_lights: Do not obstruct pedestrians who have already started crossing
If making a turn at an intersection, pay attention to pedestrians and stop if necessary

traffic_signs_at_pedestrian_crossings.blue_circular_white_lines: Mandatory sign indicating the sidewalk or pedestrian path
traffic_signs_at_pedestrian_crossings.triangular_red_frame_black_lines: Warning sign indicating a children's crossing

topics.title: Traffic Routing Elements
prohibited_actions: Placing posters or advertisements on poles, lights, road signs, or other traffic directing devices
key_road_markings: Connected / double connected lines – crossing is prohibited

overview.placement: Traffic signs are placed mainly on the right side of the road
overview.reflectivity: Reflective to ensure good visibility at night and during the day
overview.obligation: All road users must respect and abide by them

categories.shape: Triangle with vertex at the top
categories.colors: White background, black icons, red frame
categories.purpose: Alert and warn drivers of existing or potential danger on the road, street, or adjacent areas. Must be placed far enough in front of the danger so the driver can respond in time.
key_examples: Narrow road (bottleneck symbol): driver must slow down; may need to stop if oncoming vehicles are present
Low level: driver must slow down and may use a lower gear to take advantage of engine braking

signs.name: STOP sign
signs.note: Easy to identify from front and back

signs.name: Give Priority sign
signs.note: Easy to identify from front and back

subtypes.description: Indicate required or permitted direction of travel
Circular with white background, red frame, and black numbers indicating the maximum speed
Blue circle with white number indicating the minimum required speed; end of minimum speed sign ends the restriction

sign_groups: Entry prohibited to all road users
Entry prohibited to a specific type of road user (e.g. trucks, motorcycles)

subtypes.description: Indicate weight limits or specific prohibitions for trucks

subtypes.type: End of All or Some Limits
subtypes.description: Indicates end of a specific or all speed/other restrictions
Prohibits entry into a road or area
Prohibits overtaking in a specific section of road
Indicates where parking is permitted or prohibited
Various other prohibitions on specific actions

categories.purpose: Indicate important traffic conditions, provide information about routes, distances, directions, services, and places of interest

color_coding.location: Outside city limits or residential neighborhoods
Within city limits in residential areas

color_coding.refers_to: Important facilities such as airports or city centers
Farms, entertainment complexes, museums, and religious / geographic / historical places

sign_groups.group: Guidance signs to streets and neighborhoods
Guidance signs to farms, recreational complexes, and museums

categories.shapes: Same shapes as the three main categories (circle, triangle, square, rectangle)
categories.purpose: Same purpose as warning, regulatory, and guiding signs but temporarily placed on the road
sign_groups: Temporary warning signs for road works
Temporary regulatory signs (e.g. reduced speed limit in work zone)
Temporary guide signs for alternative routes
categories.note: Usually used to refer to the conduct of road works or alternative roads

topics.title: Cooperative Behavior

correct_rules_of_conduct.detail: The vehicle may only be driven if the driver is in good physical and mental condition, able to drive safely without endangering others, and holds a valid driver's license
All road users must pay attention to and respect the rights of all other road users
All drivers should drive very carefully on public roads
You must adhere to all laws, rules, and traffic lights
Always follow the instructions provided by the Traffic Department, even if they conflict with other instructions, unless they may endanger the safety of the driver or road users

topics.general_compliance_rule: All drivers must comply with all traffic regulations at all times. Drivers must also comply with orders of the Traffic Department even if these conflict with other laws. Drivers must use sound judgment and not jeopardize their own safety or the safety of other road users.

topics.title: Other Road Users – Pedestrians
pedestrian_rules_while_walking: Walk in the opposite direction of traffic if you do not obstruct traffic or endanger your safety
pedestrian_rules_when_crossing: Watch for pedestrian lights or traffic lights
Always make sure you don't obstruct traffic
Assess the speed of oncoming vehicles

pedestrian_crossing_with_traffic_lights.continuous_green: Pedestrians are allowed to cross but must also pay attention to traffic
pedestrian_crossing_with_traffic_lights.blinking_green: Those already in the street must evacuate immediately and move quickly; pedestrians approaching should not enter
pedestrian_crossing_with_traffic_lights.red: Pedestrians are not allowed to cross

topics.pedestrian_crossing_without_traffic_ligh: Sometimes indicated by adjacent white lines; pedestrians have the right of way but must monitor traffic carefully, especially in areas where drivers are allowed to drive fast
driver_behavior_near_pedestrians: Do not endanger the safety of pedestrians on sidewalks or on the side of the road
Check both sides of the road for pedestrians when approaching crossings
Slow down and be prepared to stop
Do not obstruct pedestrians who have already started crossing the street
If making a turn at an intersection, pay attention to pedestrians and stop if necessary
topics.important_fact: A car weighs 25 times the weight of a pedestrian. Always be careful and watch the traffic.

topics.title: Guided Groups of People and Animals
rules_for_groups_and_herds: Groups of people or herds of animals must wear reflective belts or vests when traveling on public roads
Large flocks should be divided into small groups to facilitate crossing the road
Herds of animals near the road must be monitored
Herds of off-road animals must be securely tied up and out of the way

topics.title: Emergency Vehicles
topics.priority: Emergency vehicles have the highest priority on emergency lanes in road traffic
topics.legal_status: Emergency vehicle drivers are not bound by any regulations or prohibitions during an emergency, but must not endanger their own safety and that of others
how_to_identify: Visual warning signals: red and blue lights
driver_obligations: Evacuate the lane for emergency vehicles as soon as possible
It is prohibited to drive directly behind emergency vehicles
Maintain a distance of at least 50 meters behind emergency vehicles
Drivers must stay on the right side of the road when approaching an emergency vehicle
You must not leave the parking lot before an emergency vehicle passes
Intersections must be evacuated quickly to avoid obstructing approaching emergency vehicles

topics.title: School Buses
topics.identification: School buses must bear markings indicating they are intended for school transportation
boarding_and_alighting_rules: School buses must stop at specific stations to enable students to get in and out
Doors must not be opened until the bus has stopped completely
Must be entered from the right side (from the sidewalk)
The school bus driver should only drive after making sure that students are safe
other_driver_rules: Other vehicles must stop when a school bus stops to load or unload students
Overtaking school buses when stopped to load or drop off students is prohibited

topics.title: Official Processions
rules: Road users should give way to official processions as soon as they announce their approach using audio and light warning devices
Stand on the right side of the road per instructions from the competent department
Do not leave until the procession has passed or per instructions issued to them
Official processions must not be interrupted or their movement obstructed by other road users

topics.title: Assessing Road Users
key_factors: Age – Special attention should be given to children and the elderly
Attention – Are people paying attention to traffic or distracted? It is important to assess potential intentions of other road users quickly to avoid accidents
topics.tip: If you are not sure about a situation, always try to make eye contact with others

characteristics: Not paying attention or not paying attention to traffic
Acting automatically most of the time
Not knowing the traffic rules and/or not complying with them
Young age – cannot accommodate traffic cases
Hearing problems and/or vision problems or other problems

topics.title: Driver's Obligations

must_not_drive_when: Injured and cannot use arms or legs properly
Under the influence of alcohol, drugs, or medication (always read the medication leaflet carefully)
ability_to_drive.reminder: Avoid distractions such as operating devices inside the vehicle, using a mobile phone, eating, and drinking while driving

before_driving: Ensure all necessary equipment is available
Ensure the vehicle is in good condition and safe to drive so that it does not obstruct or endanger other road users
Ensure there is no damage to windows, lights, mirrors, and tires
Check the condition of lights, controls, and brakes
Ensure correct sitting posture, adjust mirrors, and fasten seat belt (driver and all passengers)
while_driving: Drive on the paved area of the road and stay in the appropriate lane
Let other drivers know what you are going to do (e.g. signal before turning left or right)
prohibited_while_driving: Using visual or acoustic warning signals except in emergencies
Using warning signs with multiple tones or beeps
Turning off the engine while driving
Making noise when using the vehicle
Attaching covers or blinds to the vehicle
Placing inscriptions, drawings, or advertisements on the vehicle
Obstructing the movement of other vehicles or road users
Allowing the vehicle to roll onto a slope while the engine is turned off
Carrying people outside the passenger space
Washing or repairing the vehicle on public roads
Spitting or throwing garbage out of the vehicle while driving
Using the vehicle in processions or rallies without permission
topics.breakdown_procedure: If vehicle breaks down while driving, clear the road immediately and drive to a side street where traffic is not obstructed. During the day: place a clear warning sign within the stopping distance. During the night: secure the vehicle with red lights.
after_stopping: Ensure no one is endangered when vehicle doors are opened
Stand on the side of the sidewalk
topics.important: Ensure the vehicle is not left unlocked, the engine is not running, and the key is not left inside

topics.title: Passenger Transport
general_rules: Passenger transport is only allowed in vehicles intended for the carriage of passengers
Forbidden to transport passengers by truck or heavy machinery
Prohibited to carry passengers in the trunk of the vehicle or any external part

seat_belt_rules.general: The driver and all other passengers must use a seat belt while driving on the roads
seat_belt_rules.driver_responsibility: The driver must alert passengers to put on the seat belt
exceptions: Persons who cannot wear a seat belt for health reasons (medical evidence and permission from official authorities required)
People who are unable to wear a seat belt because of their size

transporting_children.age_12_and_under: A support belt should be placed so the seat belt is under the shoulder
transporting_children.age_10_and_under: Must not be placed in the front seat
transporting_children.exception: If the rear seats are not available, the child can be placed in the front using a child-friendly seat

topics.entry_and_exit: Passengers must exit and enter from the right side (from the sidewalk area) when the vehicle is parked on a public road

topics.title: General Driving System
general_rules: Vehicles must always be driven on the paved part of the road
The driver must obey all normal traffic lights unless directed by a traffic officer
The driver must not exceed the specified speed limit
The driver must allow other vehicles to pass safely

two_lanes_broken_line.description: Road divided into two opposite lanes by a broken line
two_lanes_broken_line.rule: Drive on the right lane; do not cross to the other lane unless overtaking

two_lanes_double_continuous_line.description: Road divided into two opposite lanes by a double continuous line
two_lanes_double_continuous_line.rule: Prohibited to cross this line to the other lane

multiple_lanes_same_direction.rule: Vehicles can go side by side; however, slower vehicles must use the far-right lane unless preparing to turn left or make a U-turn

drive_far_right_when: Other vehicles are about to overtake you
Your vehicle speed is less than the speed limit
Vehicles are coming from the opposite direction
drive_left_only_when: Necessary to prevent accidents and not to impede or endanger other road users
Driver wishes to overtake other vehicles (only if overtaking is permitted and safe)
Part of the right-hand side is blocked off (e.g. by a construction site) and there is a signal from the traffic department, security forces, or road workers
topics.driving_on_narrow_roads: When approaching jams, stay on the far-right side to maintain sufficient side distance for vehicles coming from the other direction. If necessary, stop until other vehicles from the opposite direction pass. Do not use the horn except when absolutely necessary.
topics.note: Before changing lanes, the driver must ensure this does not endanger him or others and must clearly show his intent and alert others

topics.title: Changing Lanes
when_necessary: Choose the correct lane before turning
If the driver wants to stop on the left side of the road (and only if allowed)

steps: Mirrors – Check interior and exterior side mirrors first
Signal – Give a signal (blink) to indicate intention
Shoulder – Check the blind spot by looking over the shoulder
Move – Change lanes with smooth steering motions

topics.blind_spot_warning: If you rely only on side mirrors, you risk hitting a vehicle in your blind spot. You can only see those vehicles if you look over your shoulder.

steps: Check traffic on the opposite side
Check traffic on the opposite side

topics.important: The faster you drive, the more safely you have to steer the vehicle

topics.title: Choosing the Correct Path / Lane
considerations: Ensure the turn is not blocked by traffic lights or other signals preventing the turn
Change lane or turn must be indicated by turn signals in a timely manner
Other road users must not be put at risk
Stick to road signs indicating driving directions

without_road_signs.turn_right: From the far-right side of the road
without_road_signs.turn_left_two_way_road: Move to the middle of the road; if there is a dividing line, remain to the right of the dividing line
without_road_signs.turn_left_one_way_road: From the left side of the road
without_road_signs.u_turn_two_way_road: Move to the middle of the road; if there is a dividing line, remain to the right of the dividing line
without_road_signs.u_turn_one_way_or_island: From the left side of the road (to the right of the island)

with_road_signs.turn_right: From the lane with an arrow pointing to the right
with_road_signs.turn_left: From the lane with an arrow pointing to the left
with_road_signs.u_turn: From the lane with a U-turn arrow

planning_ahead_at_multi_lane_intersectio.description: When approaching an intersection with multiple lanes for each driving direction, the correct lane depends on your direction after turning.

examples.scenario: Want to turn left, then right at next intersection
examples.action: Take the first (outermost/rightmost) of the three available left-turn lanes

examples.scenario: Want to turn left, then go straight at next intersection
examples.action: Take the second (middle) of the three available left-turn lanes

examples.scenario: Want to turn left, then turn left again at next intersection
examples.action: Take the third (innermost/leftmost) of the three available left-turn lanes

signaling_at_roundabout: Exit 1 (Turn Right): Signal right approaching and departing
Exit 2 (Go Straight): No signal approaching; signal right when exiting
Exit 3 (Turn Left): Signal left approaching; signal right when exiting
Exit 4 (Full rotation): Signal left approaching; signal right when exiting

topics.title: Turning and Reversing
turning_rules: Each turn must be signaled early enough by the turn signal
Slow down early; do not apply the brakes sharply unless absolutely necessary
Maintain a sufficient distance from the vehicle or object in front
topics.right_turn: Must be done through a narrow bend; stay on the far-right side of the road
topics.left_turn: Must be done through a wide curve; turn to the right side of the other road

rules: Reversing must be clearly indicated
Not permitted on public roads except in cases of necessity
Maximum reverse distance: 20 meters
Reverse driving is prohibited on highways
Before backing up, ensure the road is clear of vehicles and that reversing will not endanger other road users

units.title: Crossings
units.overview: Crossings are places where other roads, railways, or road users intersect. Other road users may cross from the left or right, creating dangerous situations. To avoid accidents, crossings are specially marked and secured.

rules: Vehicles must stop at the stop line or must not go beyond the level of the traffic light pole
If there is no stop line, stop where you can see the traffic lights
Must not pass the pedestrian crossing after stopping at a red light
The driver may turn right unless prohibited by a traffic light; ensure the turn can be done safely
Start driving within a reasonable time
If traffic slows or stops and the driver cannot cross the intersection, must not enter the intersection area despite the green light
If possible to stop without endangering oneself or other road users, the driver must stop
Must not cross the stop line
Stop at the stop line or at the level of the traffic light pole
If at a pedestrian crossing or railroad junction, must not cross until pedestrians or railway vehicles have cleared
Allows the driver to continue driving with great care and caution

procedure: Drive on the far-right side of the road
Stop the vehicle completely for 2–3 seconds
Move slowly at less than 15 km/h
not_allowed_when: There is a certain lane (other lane) designated for turning right
There is a signal prohibiting turning when a red light is present
turning_right_on_red.camera_note: A photo taken by the automatic monitoring camera does not necessarily mean a penalty. Every picture is manually checked by staff before imposing a penalty.

topics.title: Intersections Organized by Traffic Officer (Hand Signals)
topics.rule: When arriving at an intersection organized by a traffic officer, you must comply with the traffic officer's signs and instructions. The traffic officer has the highest priority and their instructions must be respected above all other signals including traffic lights.

stop_sign.duration: Stop for 3 seconds to keep an eye on traffic or other road users from all directions

give_way_sign.detail: If any vehicle is approaching the intersection, slow down and stop if necessary to allow it to pass. The driver must give way to other traffic on the road, giving priority to road users approaching from the right or left.

warning_sign_alerts.stop_sign_alert: Warning sign placed before the stop sign location
warning_sign_alerts.give_way_sign_alert: Warning sign placed before the give way sign location

topics.title: Right-of-Way / Priority Rules
topics.applies_at: Intersections not controlled by a traffic light or by a traffic officer

priority_order.detail: Emergency vehicles always have the highest priority while performing their duties. The driver must clear the way as soon as possible.

priority_order.rule: Vehicle closest to the intersection (not arriving simultaneously)
priority_order.detail: If two vehicles approach an intersection but not at the same time, the vehicle closest to the intersection (that enters first) has priority. The driver of the advancing vehicle must monitor traffic and assess the situation.

priority_order.rule: Right before left (arriving simultaneously on equal roads)
priority_order.detail: If two vehicles arrive at an equal intersection at the same time, the vehicle on the right side has the right-of-way. The most important thing is which direction the vehicles are approaching from, not where they are heading.

driving_straight_priority.rule_1: Vehicles driving in a straight line have priority over vehicles changing lanes
driving_straight_priority.rule_2: For vehicles traveling parallel, a driver going straight has priority over a driver wishing to change direction
driving_straight_priority.rule_3: A driver going straight ahead has the right of way to overtake drivers who are changing direction

closed_road_priority.rule: If two drivers meet on a partially closed two-way road, priority is given to the driver whose road ahead is open on the right side
closed_road_priority.additional: When a section of a two-way road is closed, the driver must comply with the instructions of the traffic department, security forces, or road workers. Both drivers must reduce speed and stop if necessary to avoid an accident.

mountain_road.rule: A driver heading down the ramp must get as close as possible to the right edge. Must allow ascending vehicles to pass without difficulty; stop completely if necessary.
mountain_road.exception: If there is an emergency parking area on the side of the ascending driver, the ascending driver must wait.

highway_entering.rule: The driver on the highway has the right of way over the driver coming from a secondary road
highway_entering.procedure: When entering from a secondary road, ensure the road is clear and give way to vehicles on the highway. Highway drivers should give the entering driver an opportunity to merge (cooperative behavior).

highway_exiting.rule: Traffic priority is given to vehicles leaving the highway to the service road. If possible, the driver on the service road must open the way for the exiting vehicle.

roundabout.rule: Drivers approaching a roundabout must give way to vehicles already traveling inside the roundabout

u_turn_at_intersection.rule: Only allowed if there is no traffic signal or traffic light preventing this
u_turn_at_intersection.priority: Priority is given to vehicles coming from any other direction; the vehicle entering the intersection first is the first to be allowed to pass

u_turn_types.closed_back_rotation: Give way to all vehicles approaching the turn; move to lane one when road is clear. Do not use parking lanes or sidewalks for U-turns.
u_turn_types.open_back_rotation: Give way to all vehicles approaching the curve; move to the second lane when road is clear to allow vehicles from the junction to enter.
u_turn_types.protected_reverse_rotation: A U-turn where the driver is protected by a dedicated signal or designated area

general_conduct_at_intersections: Approach intersections cautiously and reduce speed to allow stopping before reaching the crossing if other road users have priority
If you cannot cross an intersection, stop before reaching the crossing even with right-of-way or a green light
If there is danger of getting stuck at the intersection, avoid entering the intersection from the start
In unclear situations: make eye contact with other road users; refrain from using right of way if it helps avoid an accident
topics.importance: Priority rules play a vital role in ensuring safety on the roads of Saudi Arabia. Compliance contributes to ensuring the safety of traffic and reducing accidents and their tragic consequences.

topics.title: Pedestrian Crossings
rules: Passenger cars and bicycles are given priority over other slow-moving vehicles
Drivers must slow down and stop for pedestrians at crossings

topics.title: Railway Crossings
topics.priority: Railway vehicles have priority over all other vehicles
topics.driver_obligation: Drivers must immediately evacuate the railway tracks when a railway vehicle approaches
securing_methods: Guards – drivers must abide by the location of the barriers or guard
Traffic lights – Red or yellow indicates a train is approaching; vehicle drivers must not cross the railway line
Bell signals – Audible warning of an approaching train; vehicle drivers must not cross the railway line
topics.crossing_only_when: The sign indicates that it is safe and the driver must make sure there is no train approaching
topics.if_traffic_stops: If traffic stops or slows down and stopping at the railway lane would be dangerous, the driver must not enter the railway crossing
when_to_stop_before_railway: When there is a red or yellow light signal
When the gates are moving or are closed
When a guard signals to stop
If traffic and crosswalks do not allow crossing
prohibited: Parking of vehicles on the railways
topics.crossing_procedure: Wait until the gates are fully opened and the red light is off before entering the railway crossing

topics.title: General Speed Limits

small_vehicles.rule: Must not exceed the speed specified for the road if no other speed limiter sign is present
types: Sub-roads – according to the speed specified for the road
Highways – according to the speed specified for the road

large_vehicles.outside_city_limits: Depending on the speed specified for the road

speed_limit_signs.speed_limit_start: Traffic lights can indicate different speed limits
speed_limit_signs.speed_limit_end: A traffic sign indicating the end of the speed limit
speed_limit_signs.minimum_speed_start: Blue sign indicating the driver must not drive slower than the minimum speed
speed_limit_signs.minimum_speed_end: Sign indicating the end of the minimum speed requirement
speed_limit_signs.note: If there is no other speed limiter, you must stick to the speed limiter shown. Speed limit signs show the limit – do not feel compelled to drive at that speed.

topics.emergency_vehicles: Can exceed the speed limit, but must not endanger the safety of others

topics.title: Criteria for Choosing Driving Speed
driver_must: Always adjust speed according to general conditions and road conditions, regardless of the maximum permissible speed
Ensure safety of himself, passengers, and other road users at all times
Adapt vehicle speed to be able to stop in time in the event of a stop sign or barrier
reduce_speed_when_approaching: Intersections or any kind of crossings
When the level of vision is low
additional_situations_requiring_reduced_: If the road is not a highway
In winding places of the road
When approaching or passing a group of pedestrians
When approaching or passing animals, especially when animals show signs of anxiety and tension
topics.prohibited: Racing vehicles on public roads inside or outside city limits
topics.rule: Each case must be evaluated individually. If unsure, drive a little slower.
key_factors_to_consider: Possibility of obstacles on the road or other road users

topics.title: Drifting
topics.definition: A form of racing in which vehicles are driven at extremely high speeds of about 160 to 260 km/h on wide highways while the vehicle sways left and right. Drivers often drive close to traffic, barriers, and onlookers watching from the sides of the road without any protection.
topics.danger: Many horrific traffic accidents occur as a result of drifting

penalties.penalty: Vehicle impounded 15 days + 20,000 SAR fine + possible imprisonment
Vehicle impounded 1 month + 40,000 SAR fine + must consider imprisonment

topics.title: Obstructing Traffic and Sudden Braking
prohibited: Obstructing the movement of other vehicles by driving very slowly without a convincing reason
Suddenly slowing down or braking hard unless necessary for safety reasons
how_to_indicate_slowing_down: Brake lights at the rear of the vehicle

topics.title: Safety Distance
topics.definition: Drivers behind other vehicles must maintain sufficient distance to avoid an accident if the vehicle in front suddenly slows or stops
two_second_rule_steps: Step 1: Look for a reference point such as a traffic light, tree, mast, sign, or shadow on the road
Step 2: Start counting when the back of the vehicle in front reaches that reference point
Step 3: Count until the front of your vehicle reaches the reference point. Must count at least 2 seconds; otherwise the distance is not safe.
increase_distance_when: Bad road conditions (e.g. wet or sandy road)
Driving behind motorcycles on a one-lane road
topics.benefits_of_larger_distance: By applying a forward-looking driving style, you have more time to respond to situations and emerging dangers. Less pressure on the gas pedal; greater percentage of safety and security.

topics.title: Economic / Eco-Friendly Driving
topics.key_principle: Forward-looking driving style – take your foot off the gas pedal and let the car decelerate without pressing the brake pedal (e.g. when approaching a red traffic light). This saves fuel and reduces brake wear.

start_stop_function.with_function: Stop the car to save fuel; the feature turns off the engine when stopped and restarts automatically when foot is taken off the brake
start_stop_function.without_function: Switch off engine if idle time is longer than 20 seconds

fuel_saving_tips: Speed: Drive between 70–90 km/h; avoid speeds exceeding 100 km/h when saving fuel
Constant speed: Use cruise control as much as possible
Excess weight: Shed unnecessary weight from the vehicle
Rear window heating: Uses about 0.7 liters of fuel per 100 km; use only when the rear window is foggy; ensure it has not been started by mistake
Air conditioner: Never set too low; use the recirculation air button; always close windows when air conditioner is on
Windows: Close windows when driving at 60 km/h due to air resistance
Short distances: Avoid driving short distances; use bike, public transportation, or walk
Correct fuel: Use the correct fuel for the vehicle
Avoid rush hours and traffic jams when possible
Go straight away after starting the car
eco_friendly_behaviors: Wash the car at a special washing station that recycles water
Maintain the car regularly; use a container to collect old oil and dispose of it correctly – do not let it contaminate the floor
Car sharing: As many people as possible in one car
Install a purifier in the car if possible

topics.title: Driving Near Stationary Vehicles and Objects
when_not_to_pass: If other road users are obstructed or endangered
In the event of causing damage to fixed objects
When people exit or enter railway vehicles on one side of the road

procedure_when_obstacle_in_path.evaluate: Is there movement coming? Is there enough space for passage?
procedure_when_obstacle_in_path.decide: Decide to either pass or stop
procedure_when_obstacle_in_path.act: Act according to your decision: Move or stop

steps: Mirrors: Check interior and left side mirrors to see vehicles behind you
Shoulder: Check the blind spot on the left side of your vehicle
Speed: Adapt the speed (speed up if obstacle can be crossed quickly; slow down if narrow)
Move: Move to the left side and make sure there is enough lateral distance to pass the obstacle. Drive smoothly.

near_parked_vehicles.lateral_distance: Be sure to move away from the side of parked vehicles (at 50 km/h, you need about 1 meter – approximately the space needed to open a vehicle door)
near_parked_vehicles.on_two_way_roads: May need to slow down or stop when traffic is coming from the other direction
near_parked_vehicles.watch_for: Vehicles that are about to move
near_parked_vehicles.rule: The required lateral distance depends on driving speed – the faster you are, the greater the distance needed from parked vehicles

topics.right_of_way_note: The driver whose road is open on the right side has the right of way

topics.title: Overtaking Moving Vehicles
overtake_on_right_when: The driver in front intends to turn left
The road is divided into more than two lanes heading in the same direction
rules_for_vehicle_being_overtaken: Must drive on the far-right side of the road
Must indicate to the other driver that overtaking is permitted
Must reduce speed if overtaken by a group of vehicles

topics.title: Overtaking Prohibitions
prohibited_locations: On curved roads and dangerous curves
When driving in the opposite direction to other vehicles
When visibility on roads is insufficient or weak
When there is a 'No overtaking' traffic sign
When there are solid lines between tracks
prohibited_situations: When you cannot drive significantly faster than the vehicle in front of you
If the speed limit would be exceeded while overtaking
If a vehicle in front of you begins to overtake another vehicle ahead of it
If a vehicle behind you begins to overtake your vehicle
topics.warning: There are many things that must be taken into account when overtaking. Do not try to overtake another vehicle if you are in doubt.

topics.title: Requirements for Safe Overtaking
before_overtaking_checklist: 1. Check your speed: need an appropriate speed difference compared to the vehicle ahead (good difference: at least 20 km/h but not exceeding the speed limit)
2. Check the space next to the vehicle you want to overtake: maintain a safe lateral distance; ensure the vehicle in front is not starting to overtake another vehicle
3. Check the mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure no one is overtaking you
4. Check the road ahead: no obstructing oncoming traffic, no curves, crossings, or obstacles
5. Ensure there is space on the right side of the road to return to it after overtaking

overtaking_procedure.see: Speed? Way ahead? Space to return to right lane?
overtaking_procedure.assess: Is overtaking allowed? Is it safe?
overtaking_procedure.decide: Overtake (start MSSSM) or stay behind within a safe distance
overtaking_procedure.mirrors: Check left and side mirrors for vehicles behind you
overtaking_procedure.shoulder: Check blind spot on left side
overtaking_procedure.speed: Accelerate (exceed the vehicle ahead's speed as quickly as possible without exceeding the speed limit)
overtaking_procedure.move: Move to the left side; ensure enough lateral space for the vehicle being overtaken; drive smoothly
overtaking_procedure.return: Turn right when you can see the overtaken vehicle in the interior mirror; steer smoothly

topics.title: Stopping the Vehicle

definitions.pause: Stopping the vehicle and continuing to park for a short and limited period
definitions.parking: Stop the vehicle and leave it parked

parking_rules: Vehicles must be parked on the side of the road or on the side of the sidewalk parallel to it
In another way if there is a sign indicating this
Parallel to the side of the road or sidewalk unless a sign indicates otherwise

parking_signs.yellow_area_on_road: Parking is prohibited; prohibition ends at the first turn after the sign
parking_signs.waiting_allowed_no_parking: Waiting is allowed, parking is not allowed
parking_signs.no_standing_or_waiting: No standing or waiting at all

prohibited_at: Within 1.5 meters of a children's school crossing
Within 20 meters of tunnels (on either side)
On top of the road (crest of a hill)
Within 15 meters of a traffic light
Within 7 meters of a fire hydrant
In front of entrances or exits
In places designated for a specific category of vehicle (e.g. disabled parking)
In the opposite direction of traffic
In the middle of the road

broken_down_vehicle.general: Park off the road if possible
broken_down_vehicle.during_day: Place clear warning signs within the stopping distance
broken_down_vehicle.at_night: Place red lights on the vehicle to avoid collisions with other vehicles
broken_down_vehicle.highway_note: On public roads outside the city, if parked vehicles pose a danger to public safety, additional precautions must be taken

topics.trucks_triple_deflectors: Truck drivers must place one or more triple deflectors (each side 30 cm long) on the road behind the truck and on the left side if parked at night out of town on public roads

topics.title: Using Vehicle Headlights

front.name: Front fog lights
front.function: Visibility in fog, snow, or heavy rain (only on some vehicles)

rear.name: Rear lights (taillights)
rear.function: Indicate presence of vehicle from behind

rear.name: Brake lights (stop lights)
rear.function: Appear every time the brake pedal is depressed

rear.name: Reverse lights
rear.function: Appear only when the transmission is in reverse ('R') position

turn_signals.function: Indicate direction of turn; appear when blinker is activated

hazard_warning_lights.function: All turn signals flash simultaneously to indicate hazard

usage_rules.at_night: Drivers must use vehicle headlights while driving at night regardless of whether the road is equipped with general lighting
usage_rules.during_day: Must use headlights during thick fog or sandstorms obscuring vision

low_beams_required_when: In cases where high beams are prohibited and position lights do not provide sufficient visibility
When position lights are not sufficient for other road users to see the vehicle in time
When fog is present and the vehicle is not equipped with fog lights
high_beams_prohibited: Within city limits (always use regular/low beam lights inside cities)
When there are oncoming vehicles on the opposite side (turn off at sufficient distance)
When driving less than 50 meters behind other vehicles
In all cases that may cause great inconvenience to other road users
In all cases that may cause great inconvenience to users of a waterway or railway parallel to the road

fog_lights_rules.front_fog_lights: Must be used in fog, snowfall, or heavy rain
fog_lights_rules.rear_fog_lights: Use only when there is fog, snow, or heavy rain; ensure not too bright; use only when no vehicles are driving directly behind you
rear_lights_when: On roads without general lighting at night
On roads without general lighting during the day when there is fog, heavy rain, or sandstorm

other_light_rules.flashing_lights: Prohibited to use without permission from the Traffic Department
other_light_rules.red_reflective_lights: Prohibited to use from the center of the vehicle to the front of the vehicle
other_light_rules.white_lights_from_rear: Use of white lights from the center of the vehicle to the rear is prohibited, except number plate lights and reverse lights

lights.meaning: STOP IMMEDIATELY! Have a look at your vehicle manual.
Something is not right. Inspect the vehicle as soon as possible and do not ignore it for too long.

fuel_indicator.rule: Must fill the fuel tank when the indicator is at a quarter of the tank
fuel_indicator.reason: Running out of fuel on the road puts your life and the lives of others at risk

topics.title: Clear View / Demisting

controls.function: Adjusts the direction of the fan/air flow
Circulates air inside the vehicle (e.g. when driving in tunnels)
Adjusts the strength of the fan
Heats the rear window to clear fog/condensation
Adjusts the temperature of the air flow
Purifies the air and extracts water vapor

topics.demisting_tip: To clear fog from the front window, turn all switches clockwise to the far right

quiz_bank.question: What is the minimum age to obtain a private driving license in Saudi Arabia?
quiz_bank.explanation: You must be at least 18 years old. A temporary permit can be issued from age 17 for a maximum of one year.

quiz_bank.question: How long is a private driving license valid for?
quiz_bank.explanation: A private driver's license is valid for a maximum of 10 years.

quiz_bank.question: What is the maximum number of passengers (including driver) allowed with a private license?
quiz_bank.explanation: A private license allows carrying a maximum of 9 passengers including the driver.

quiz_bank.question: What is the minimum age for a public driving license?
quiz_bank.explanation: You must be at least 20 years old to obtain a public driving license.

quiz_bank.question: What is the stopping distance at 50 km/h on a dry road?
quiz_bank.explanation: At 50 km/h: reaction distance is 15m + braking distance is 25m = stopping distance of 40m.

quiz_bank.question: What is the stopping distance at 100 km/h on a dry road?
quiz_bank.explanation: At 100 km/h: reaction distance 30m + braking distance 100m = 130m stopping distance.

quiz_bank.question: What is the reaction time assumed in the standard stopping distance formula?
quiz_bank.explanation: Standard reaction time is assumed to be 1 second in stopping distance calculations.

quiz_bank.question: When does the reaction distance become longer?
quiz_bank.explanation: Reaction distance increases at high speeds, if you are distracted or tired, or under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

quiz_bank.question: What number do you call for the Red Crescent in an accident with injuries?
quiz_bank.explanation: Call the Red Crescent at 997 for accidents with injuries.

quiz_bank.question: What is the maximum damage amount for an accident to be classified as 'minor'?
quiz_bank.explanation: A minor accident involves property damage not exceeding 5,000 SAR and injuries not requiring hospitalization.

quiz_bank.question: How many points result in the withdrawal of a driver's license?
quiz_bank.explanation: The driver's license is withdrawn when the total number of points reaches 24.

quiz_bank.question: How many points are assigned for driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs?
quiz_bank.explanation: Driving under the influence carries the maximum penalty of 24 points – enough to withdraw the license immediately.

quiz_bank.question: How many points are assigned for running a red light?
quiz_bank.explanation: Not stopping while a red light is on carries 12 points.

quiz_bank.question: How many points for not wearing a seat belt?
quiz_bank.explanation: Not wearing a seat belt carries 2 points.

quiz_bank.question: What is the fine for drifting on the FIRST offense?
quiz_bank.explanation: The first drifting offense: vehicle impounded 15 days + 20,000 SAR fine + possible imprisonment.

quiz_bank.question: What happens on the THIRD drifting offense?
quiz_bank.explanation: Third drifting offense results in confiscation of the vehicle and a 60,000 SAR fine.

quiz_bank.question: How many days does the driver have to pay the minimum fine before the maximum is imposed?
quiz_bank.explanation: The violating driver may pay the minimum fine within a maximum period of 30 days from the date of the violation.

quiz_bank.question: How long is the license withdrawn for the FIRST time the point limit is reached in one Hijri year?
quiz_bank.explanation: For the first time in one Hijri year, the driver's license is withdrawn for 3 months.

quiz_bank.question: What shape are warning signs?
quiz_bank.explanation: Warning signs are triangular with vertex at the top, white background, black icons, and red frame.

quiz_bank.question: What does a blue circular regulatory sign indicate?
quiz_bank.explanation: Blue circular signs indicate a mandatory obligation (e.g. minimum speed, compulsory direction).

quiz_bank.question: What color are temporary work area signs?
quiz_bank.explanation: Temporary work area signs are yellow with a red frame.

quiz_bank.question: What color background indicates a guide sign to cities and villages outside city limits?
quiz_bank.explanation: Blue background with white letters indicates guide signs outside city limits, referring to cities and villages.

quiz_bank.question: What is the minimum distance to maintain behind an emergency vehicle?
quiz_bank.explanation: It is prohibited to drive directly behind emergency vehicles. A distance of at least 50 meters must be maintained.

quiz_bank.question: What must all other vehicles do when a school bus stops to let students in or out?
quiz_bank.explanation: All vehicles must stop and overtaking a stopped school bus is prohibited.

quiz_bank.question: At what age may children NOT sit in the front seat?
quiz_bank.explanation: Children under 10 must not be in the front seat unless the rear seats are unavailable (with child-friendly seat).

quiz_bank.question: Who must wear a seat belt?
quiz_bank.explanation: The driver and all other passengers must use a seat belt while driving on the roads.

quiz_bank.question: What does the abbreviation MSSSM stand for when changing lanes?
quiz_bank.explanation: MSSSM: Mirrors → Signal → Shoulder (blind spot check) → Speed → Move. This applies to changing lanes and overtaking.

quiz_bank.question: What is the maximum permitted reversing distance on a public road?
quiz_bank.explanation: Not permissible to drive backwards for more than 20 meters. Prohibited entirely on highways.

quiz_bank.question: What should you do when the traffic light turns yellow/orange?
options: Accelerate to cross the intersection quickly
Stop if possible without endangering yourself or others
quiz_bank.correct_answer: Stop if possible without endangering yourself or others
quiz_bank.explanation: When the light turns yellow/orange, stop if it is possible to do so safely; do not cross the stop line.

quiz_bank.question: What is the required speed when turning right on a red light?
quiz_bank.explanation: When turning right at a red light, your speed must be less than 15 km/h and you must stop completely for 2–3 seconds first.

quiz_bank.question: At an uncontrolled equal intersection, two cars arrive at the same time. Which has priority?
quiz_bank.explanation: The right-before-left rule: if two vehicles arrive at an equal intersection simultaneously, the vehicle on the right has right-of-way.

quiz_bank.question: Who has priority between a vehicle on the highway and one entering from a secondary road?
options: The vehicle on the secondary road
quiz_bank.explanation: The driver on the highway always has the right of way over the driver coming from a secondary road.

quiz_bank.question: Who has priority at a roundabout?
options: The vehicle already inside the roundabout
quiz_bank.correct_answer: The vehicle already inside the roundabout
quiz_bank.explanation: Drivers approaching a roundabout must give way to vehicles already traveling inside the roundabout.

quiz_bank.question: What is prohibited at railway crossings?
quiz_bank.explanation: It is prohibited to stop on rails, park on railways, or drive along the rails.

quiz_bank.question: What is the maximum speed for large vehicles within city roads?
quiz_bank.explanation: Drivers of large vehicles must not exceed 50 km/h on city roads within cities.

quiz_bank.question: What is the minimum following distance (two-second rule)?
quiz_bank.explanation: The minimum distance to drive behind another vehicle is two seconds (the two-second rule).

quiz_bank.question: What speed range is considered optimal for fuel saving?
quiz_bank.explanation: Speed between 70 to 90 km/h saves fuel. Avoid driving at any speed exceeding 100 km/h when trying to save fuel.

quiz_bank.question: On which side must you normally overtake another vehicle?
quiz_bank.explanation: Vehicles must normally be overtaken on the left side of the road.

quiz_bank.question: Overtaking is prohibited on which of the following?
quiz_bank.explanation: Overtaking is prohibited at pedestrian crossings, intersections, railway lanes, bridges, curves, slippery roads, etc.

quiz_bank.question: When are high beams prohibited within city limits?
quiz_bank.explanation: Within city limits, drivers must always use regular low beam lights. High beams are always prohibited in cities.

quiz_bank.question: What is the minimum distance you must park from a fire hydrant?
quiz_bank.explanation: It is forbidden to stop the vehicle within 7 meters of a fire hydrant.

quiz_bank.question: What is the minimum distance to park from a traffic light?
quiz_bank.explanation: It is forbidden to stop the vehicle at a distance of less than 15 meters from a traffic light.

quiz_bank.question: What is the minimum distance to park from a tunnel or bridge?
quiz_bank.explanation: It is prohibited to park within 20 meters of tunnels or bridges, or on bridges themselves.

quiz_bank.question: What does a RED dashboard warning light mean?
options: Stop immediately and consult vehicle manual
quiz_bank.correct_answer: Stop immediately and consult vehicle manual
quiz_bank.explanation: A red dashboard warning light means stop immediately and consult the vehicle manual.

quiz_bank.question: When should you fill the fuel tank according to the handbook?
options: When the fuel indicator is at half
When the fuel indicator is at a quarter
When the low fuel warning light comes on
When the tank is completely empty
quiz_bank.correct_answer: When the fuel indicator is at a quarter
quiz_bank.explanation: You must fill the fuel tank when the indicator is at a quarter of the tank to avoid running out on the road.

quiz_bank.question: A traffic officer tells you to stop at a green light. What should you do?
options: Proceed because the light is green
Stop and follow the officer's instructions
Flash headlights to warn the officer
quiz_bank.correct_answer: Stop and follow the officer's instructions
quiz_bank.explanation: Traffic officer instructions take priority over all traffic regulations including traffic lights. Always follow the officer's instructions.

quiz_bank.question: What must a driver do if their vehicle breaks down on the road?
options: Leave the vehicle and wait on the sidewalk
Clear the road immediately; place warning signs (day) or red lights (night)
Call for help and stay in the vehicle
Leave the vehicle running with hazard lights on
quiz_bank.correct_answer: Clear the road immediately; place warning signs (day) or red lights (night)
quiz_bank.explanation: If the vehicle breaks down, clear the road immediately and drive to a side street. During the day: place a clear warning sign. At night: secure the vehicle with red lights.

quiz_bank.question: How long must you stop at a STOP sign?
quiz_bank.explanation: Stop completely for 3 seconds to keep an eye on traffic or other road users from all directions.

quiz_bank.question: What does a double continuous line between two lanes mean?
options: You are prohibited from crossing to the other lane
quiz_bank.correct_answer: You are prohibited from crossing to the other lane
quiz_bank.explanation: A double continuous line means drivers are prohibited from crossing this line to the other lane.

quiz_bank.question: At what speed range is drifting typically performed?
quiz_bank.explanation: Drifting is a form of racing in which vehicles are driven at extremely high speeds of about 160 to 260 km/h on wide highways.
